title: After Hurricane Harvey: How Thousands of Homeowners Lost Deposits to Contractor Fraud
excerpt: In the aftermath of Hurricane Harvey, unlicensed contractors swept through Houston collecting deposits for repairs they never intended to complete. The pattern — and what escrow would have changed.

title: Hurricane Ian's Second Wave: Roofing Scammers Who Preyed on Southwest Florida
excerpt: Following Hurricane Ian's destruction, a wave of fraudulent roofing contractors targeted Southwest Florida homeowners — taking money upfront and vanishing before a single shingle was laid.

title: Unlicensed Contractors Swarmed California Wildfire Victims for Millions
excerpt: After California's devastating wildfires, the Contractors State License Board conducted sting operations that caught dozens of unlicensed operators targeting displaced homeowners. Many demanded illegal upfront deposits before vanishing or performing dangerous, substandard work.

title: The Atlanta Pool Builder Who Left Homeowners With Empty Yards and Drained Deposits
excerpt: Rick McDermott's Aqua Blue Pools collected large deposits from homeowners across metro Atlanta but left projects unfinished or never started. Prosecutors charged him after families across multiple counties lost their money to abandoned pool construction contracts.

title: The Bonney Lake Contractor Who Took Approaching $1M From Homeowners
excerpt: Construction Kings, based in Bonney Lake, Washington, collected large deposits for home renovation and construction projects, then failed to complete the work. State regulators, local police, and a multistate federal probe pursued the case after 26 or more homeowners reported losses.

title: The Wichita Contractor Ordered to Pay Over $500,000 After Taking Homeowner Deposits
excerpt: Chad E. Smith, a Wichita-area contractor, collected large deposits from homeowners for remodeling and construction projects, then failed to complete the work or refund the money. He was convicted on 25 counts and ordered to pay over $500,000 in restitution.

title: The Centerville Contractor Who Took Over $400,000 From Homeowners
excerpt: Edson Lins, an unlicensed Centerville, Utah contractor, collected large deposits for home construction and remodeling projects, then failed to complete the work, leaving families out hundreds of thousands of dollars. State prosecutors charged him with multiple felony counts after homeowner complaints mounted.

title: The Solar Company That Took Deposits and Left Panels Unconnected Across Georgia
excerpt: Vision Solar collected thousands from Georgia and multi-state homeowners for rooftop solar installations that were never completed or connected to the grid. Customers were left paying loans on systems that produced no power.

title: The Hurricane Michael Contractor Who Left Panhandle Homes in Ruins
excerpt: After Hurricane Michael devastated Florida's Panhandle in 2018, desperate homeowners handed deposits to contractors promising rebuilds. Many were left with unfinished shells, drained savings, and no recourse as storm-chasing operators collected cash and moved on.

title: The Omaha Contractors Who Took Storm Deposits and Vanished
excerpt: Two Omaha-area contractors collected deposits from homeowners for siding and roofing repairs after severe storms, then failed to complete the work or return the money. Authorities charged both after victims came forward with losses.

title: The Denver Contractor Who Stole $1.4M and Left Homes in Ruins
excerpt: Avi Schwalb, owner of Schwalb Builders, was convicted on 47 felony counts and sentenced to 10 years for a home-remodeling scheme that took over $1.4 million from Denver-area homeowners. Many families paid large deposits only to see projects abandoned after demolition, leaving their homes damaged and uninhabitable.

title: The Fort Worth Couple Who Took $4.8M for Custom Homes They Never Finished
excerpt: Christopher and Raquelle Judge marketed their company Judge DFW as a one-stop custom home shop, but federal prosecutors say they abandoned projects after collecting millions in installment payments. More than 40 North Texas homeowners were left with unfinished homes and roughly $4.8 million in losses.

title: The Niagara County Contractor Who Stole $230K in Deposits for Work He Never Did
excerpt: Newfane contractor Nathaniel Wagner took large upfront deposits from more than a dozen Western New York homeowners, then spent the money on personal expenses instead of building the barns, garages, and decks he promised. He was sentenced to four to eight years in prison and ordered to repay over $453,000.
